title: Scheduler instrumentation for queueing + batching (queue wait, batch assembly, drops, trace correlation)
creator: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Goal
Add production-safe scheduler instrumentation needed for Q1 2026 perf baselines and ongoing regression triage. We need to explain TTFT/TPOT changes by breaking latency into: (a) queueing, (b) batch formation/assembly, and (c) execution time. Also add drop/load-shed counters to make overload behavior attributable and comparable across runs.

Context
Perf suite runs have repeatedly shown p95/p99 TTFT shifts that are hard to attribute (scheduler changes vs kernel changes vs cluster noise). Current runtime logs do not provide consistent, low-overhead measurements of scheduler internals, and traces lack a reliable correlation ID that ties a request across: client → gateway → runtime → GPU execution spans.

Scope
1) Metrics (runtime-exported; prod safe)
- queue_wait_ms: time from request enqueued → selected into a batch.
- batch_assembly_ms: time spent building the batch (tokenization already excluded; focus on scheduler bookkeeping + batching decisions).
- batch_size_{requests,tokens_prefill,tokens_decode}: distributions (histograms) to understand continuous batching behavior and tail effects.
- inflight_queue_depth: sampled gauge (per worker) to detect backpressure regimes.
- load_shed_count + load_shed_reason: counters for requests dropped/failed fast due to overload guardrails.
- timeout_count (scheduler-side): requests that expired while waiting in queue (if applicable).

2) Tagging / cardinality constraints
- Required tags: model_id, model_family, workload_id, region, gpu_sku, scheduler_policy_id, runtime_build, run_id.
- Optional tags (sampled only): route, customer_tier.
- Hard rule: no per-request IDs as metric tags. Correlation IDs must be log/trace-only.

3) Correlation IDs for traces
- Introduce scheduler_correlation_id as a deterministic ID per request (UUIDv4 ok) that is:
  - passed into trace spans (server-side)
  - logged in structured scheduler logs at key transitions (enqueue, batch-assign, execute-start, first-token, done)
  - included in perf suite artifacts for sampled requests (see sampling plan)
- Ensure it is compatible with existing trace propagation headers from the gateway (if present). If upstream already provides trace_id, store both (trace_id + scheduler_correlation_id) and document the join key.

4) Logging (debug-only; perf-run friendly)
- Provide a debug dump mode (guarded by config + sampling) that emits a compact JSON line per request with:
  - timestamps for enqueue/batch-assign/execute-start/first-token/done
  - batch_id
  - batch_size (req/tokens)
  - load-shed reason (if applicable)
  - scheduler policy snapshot hash
This is primarily for benchmark runs and profiler correlation; must be disabled by default in production.

Non-goals
- Not implementing new scheduling heuristics; only instrumentation + minimal plumbing.
- Not adding per-token tracing (too expensive).

Acceptance criteria
- Metrics appear in the perf baseline dashboards and can be filtered by run_id/model/workload.
- For a representative suite run, we can decompose TTFT into queue_wait_ms + batch_assembly_ms + execute_to_first_token_ms (the last component derived from traces, not necessarily a metric).
- Overhead: <1% throughput impact on steady-state decode at typical production concurrency, verified on at least one A100 and one H100 run.
- Cardinality: metrics backend does not show a significant new series explosion; tags validated with Observability.
- Load-shed counters align with existing HTTP error responses (no double-counting).

Implementation notes / plan
- Add timestamps at scheduler state transitions using a monotonic clock.
- Define histograms with sane buckets for queue_wait_ms (0–5s), batch_assembly_ms (0–200ms), and batch sizes.
- Wire to runtime metrics exporter (same path used by existing runtime pXX latency metrics).
- Add a sampling knob for structured scheduler logs: sample_rate (default 0), max_qps (default 0), and allowlist for perf runs (workload_id/run_id).
- Add a config flag to include scheduler_correlation_id into trace spans (default on when tracing is on).

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: performance overhead from per-request timestamping/logging.
  - Mitigation: timestamping only; logs are sampling-gated and off by default.
- Risk: metric tag cardinality growth.
  - Mitigation: keep required tags limited; forbid request_id; sample route/tier tags.
- Risk: inconsistent measurement boundaries (TTFT definitions).
  - Mitigation: document boundaries in Confluence methodology; align with company perf regression policy.

Links
- Umbrella: ENG-4821 (Q1 2026 perf baseline kickoff and scope)
- Schema: ENG-4822 (run manifest/results schema)
- Related runtime PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-21503-scheduler-queue-time-and-batch-assembly-metrics.json
- Dashboard work: ENG-4829

comments: 2025-12-05 — Sofia Ivanova: Drafted metric list + tag set. Biggest open question is whether we can compute execute_to_first_token purely from traces or if we need a metric. Leaning traces to avoid high-cardinality per-phase metrics.

2025-12-09 — Allison Grant: Please do NOT tag metrics with correlation IDs. Keep tags to model/workload/region/SKU/build/run_id at most. Route + tier are ok only if sampled or constrained to a small enum. Also confirm histogram buckets match existing latency bucket conventions.

2025-12-12 — Sean Gallagher: For load shedding, we need explicit reasons (queue_full, max_inflight, deadline_exceeded) so SRE can distinguish regressions from capacity issues. Also ensure counters match HTTP 429 vs 503 mapping and don't double count retries.

2025-12-18 — Sofia Ivanova: Implemented queue_wait_ms + batch_assembly_ms timestamps behind feature flag; started wiring histograms. Added initial correlation_id plumbing to trace spans. Working on log sampling guardrails next.

2026-01-07 — Marcus Reed: Bench harness can pass run_id/workload_id tags via env; please ensure runtime accepts these and exports them so we can join runs to manifests. Also request a 'scheduler_policy_id' string tag for baseline comparisons.

2026-01-14 — Sofia Ivanova: Added scheduler_policy_id tag + batch_size histograms (req/tokens). Load_shed counters now include reason. Debug JSON log dump exists but default sample_rate=0. Pushed PR for review.

2026-01-22 — Connor O'Brien: For release gating, we need these metrics reliably exported in CI perf-canary. Make sure metrics are emitted even when tracing is disabled (queue/batch metrics should not depend on tracing).

2026-02-04 — Sofia Ivanova: Landed in runtime-1.18 via PR-21503. Verified overhead on H100 decode workload (~0.4% tokens/s delta, within noise). Dashboards can now break down TTFT shifts into queue vs batch assembly, which helped explain the long-prefill p99 incident thread.
